title: Graceful KV deallocation: epochal quiesce windows for continuous batching and GPU memory compaction
creator: Aisha Morgan
description:
Problem: Continuous batching and aggressive KV reclamation reduce GPU memory but risk serving correctness when in-flight requests reference recently reclaimed prefix/kvs. Existing LRU/TTL strategies either leave stale entries for too long (wasting memory) or reclaim too eagerly (risking incorrect outputs or crashes).

Proposal: Implement an epochal quiesce-based deallocation protocol that combines soft TTL, tenant-aware quotas, and a short deterministic quiesce window per reclaim epoch. During each epoch we will: mark candidate entries, quiesce new allocations that may alias reclaimed slabs, wait for in-flight batch references to drain via per-batch fencing, and then perform slab compaction/defragmentation. This gives deterministic safety bounds for correctness while enabling more aggressive memory compaction between epochs.
acceptance_criteria: No regression in model output correctness on our deterministic prompt suite after reclamation under continuous-batching workloads (baseline: current master).
Peak GPU memory usage reduced by >= 12% on long-tail prefix workloads (24-hour trace replay) compared to current TTL-only reclamation.
End-to-end P99 latency increase <= 5% under target throughput during reclamation epochs.
Protocol invariants enforced: (1) in-flight references never point to reclaimed physical pages, (2) reclaimed slab addresses are not reused until post-quiesce fence acknowledgement.
Automated chaos/fuzz harness passes (no use-after-free) across 1M randomized batch traces.
design_decisions: Use epoch counters (uint64) stored with each slab header instead of per-entry reference counting to minimize atomic ops during hot-path access.
Combine soft TTL with a tenant quota watermark: entries under the watermark use LRU for aging, above watermark use epochal marking to prioritize compaction.
Implement per-batch fences: each request batch reads current epoch before KV lookups; reclamation waits for fence acknowledgements from active batch trackers before physical free.
Avoid global stop-the-world drains; rely on short quiesce windows (configurable, default 250ms) to bound tail-safety while allowing high throughput.
Prefetch / forward-compat: reclaimed address space is added to a quarantine ring buffer for one additional epoch to reduce fragmentation-induced aliasing.
Expose conservative and aggressive modes via runtime flags for dedicated vs hosted tiers.
implementation_notes: Create epoch_manager service within runtime memory manager responsible for issuing epoch increments and tracking active batch IDs.
Modify KV slab header layout: add epoch_tag (8 bytes) and quarantine_flag (1 byte); keep header <= 64 bytes to preserve cache friendliness.
Hot-path KV lookup does two reads: value pointer and slab.epoch_tag; if mismatch with batch_epoch, treat as miss and trigger safe reload path (fast).
Batch lifecycle: request handler attaches a transient batch token to context; token registration increments per-worker active_batch counter; deregistration decrements.
Compaction step sequence: mark -> wait-for-quiesce -> migrate live prefixes to new slab region -> update indirections atomically -> free old slab back to GPU allocator.
Metrics to add: epoch_active_batches, epoch_quiesce_duration_ms, quarantine_ring_fill, reclaimed_bytes_per_epoch, page_alias_events.
Implementation will be in two PRs: 1) epoch manager + batch fencing + tests; 2) slab compaction and quarantine ring + perf tuning.
tests: Unit: epoch manager increment/decrement semantics, fence ack/timeout behavior.
Integration: replay 24-hour production prefix trace under continuous-batching harness; verify correctness suite and memory curve.
Load: 500 concurrent tenants at sustained 60k rps with mixed sequence lengths (32/512/2048) to validate latency SLOs during compaction epochs.
Fuzz: randomized interleaving of batch start/stop, TTL expiry, and slab migrations for 1M iterations in fuzzbench harness.
Safety: small-scale synthetic model that asserts pointer validity on KV reads (ASAN in CI for native builds).
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'epochal_reclaim'. Default off in hosted; opt-in in Dedicated for initial trials.
Phase 1 (canary): enable on 2%) of requests in Dev region for 48h; monitor correctness, GPU mem, P99 latency.
Phase 2 (staged): increase to 20% across non-critical models; run 7-day trace replay nightly and validate metrics.
Phase 3 (production): enable by default for Dedicated customers after 4 weeks of stable canaries and no regression.
Rollback: immediate disable of epochal_reclaim flag rolls back to TTL-only reclamation and triggers emergency compaction drain if needed.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Aisha Morgan: Initial design sketch posted to Confluence; raised concern about per-batch counter overhead on hot-path. Decided to use epoch tag reads instead of refcount increments.

2025-01-20 - Liam Chen: Prototype epoch_manager implemented; microbenchmarks show +1.3% CPU on hot-path for small models. Working on reducing header reads by packing epoch tag alongside pointer to minimize loads.
2025-01-28 - Design review: PM (Rohit Das) requested SLA targets for Hosted; added conservative mode and explicit release gating. Also added quarantine ring to reduce aliasing.
2025-02-02 - Engineering review: noted potential interaction with KV prefetch; added dependency ENG-30642 for prefetch-backpressure integration.
2025-02-04 - QA: Started fuzz runs on CI with ASAN; discovered rare timeout where a batch fence ack is delayed > 2s under extreme GC; mitigation: backoff/force-drain path added.
